projectSettingsDialog.viewerSharedSettings: You can view this shared project. Its name, colour and icon are the same for everyone in it, and only an owner or editor can change them.
projectSettingsDialog.folderOptionalLinkOne: A folder is optional. Link one when the project has files on this computer, such as code or documents.
projectSettingsDialog.howProjectsTaskEstimates: How this project's task estimates count.
projectSettingsDialog.autoSoftwareWhenLinked: Auto is software when the linked folder is a Git repository. For software projects AI writes tasks for coding agents; for general ones, for the person doing them.
projectSettingsDialog.labelsProjectsTasksColour: The labels on this project's tasks. A colour tells them apart on the Board.
projectSettingsDialog.taskTypesDescription: The kinds of task in this project. Each task can have one, shown by its icon on cards and rows.
projectSettingsDialog.doneTasksMoveArchive: Done tasks move to the archive this many days after they're finished. 0 turns it off.
projectSettingsDialog.linkFolderLetAgents: Link a folder to let agents work on this project.
projectSettingsDialog.howAgentsPickUp: How agents pick up this project's tasks. Every run works on its own copy, and nothing reaches your folder until you accept it.
projectSettingsDialog.reviewBeforeMeHint: Each finished piece of work with changes is reviewed by a second run before it waits for you. The reviewer uses a copy of its own, changes nothing, and counts towards usage limits. Its findings show in Review changes.
projectSettingsDialog.agentsPlanFirstHint: Each task's agent sends a plan and waits for your approval before it changes anything, unless the task says otherwise. A run waits as long as its plan does, and its copy stays in use meanwhile, counting towards the copies {{brand}} prepares ahead.
projectSettingsDialog.startsBuiltAgentsQueued: Starts built-in agents on queued tasks by themselves, up to the limit below.
projectSettingsDialog.up4EachRun: Up to 4: each run needs its own workspace.
projectSettingsDialog.agentsNormallyUseModel: A run uses the model chosen when it was queued, else this, else Settings › Agents. Keys and addresses still come from Settings › AI.
projectSettingsDialog.howWorkDoneProject: How work is done in this project: code style, commands to run, things to avoid. Every agent gets these with each task, so you never paste them into a task again.
projectSettingsDialog.howWorkspacePrepared: How a new agent workspace gets its dependencies before the agent starts. {{brand}} runs it once, in the new workspace only, and the agent does not start until it finishes.
projectSettingsDialog.setupNoLockfile: No lockfile or .NET solution found, so nothing will run.
projectSettingsDialog.setupCommandHint: Runs in each new workspace with CI=1 set, so installers do not prompt. Saved when you leave the field.
projectSettingsDialog.setupCommandBlank: Enter a command, or choose Automatic or Off.
projectSettingsDialog.setupOffHint: Nothing is installed. The agent works with whatever the workspace already contains.
projectSettingsDialog.savedWhenLeaveField: Saved when you leave the field. Agents read them; they don't give agents any more access.
projectSettingsDialog.conventionsExample:
- Run npm test before committing
- Use tabs, not spaces
projectSettingsDialog.fieldsDescription: Fields of this project's own, such as a client or a room, on every task. Text, Number, Date, Choice, Choices or Checkbox.
projectSettingsDialog.tokenLimitsDescription: Optional limits for the built-in agent, counted in tokens in and out. At a limit, no new run starts and a running one stops at its next turn, with its work kept for review. Limits reset at midnight and on the first of the month.
projectSettingsDialog.githubDescription: Optional. With a repository, a task can link an issue as #123, and Import tasks can bring in its issues. Nothing is sent to GitHub until you link or import.
projectSettingsDialog.githubRepositoryHint: Its owner and name, or its github.com address. Saved when you leave the field.
projectSettingsDialog.projectPeopleDescription: People who only work on this project. They're offered only here, and go when the project is removed. Everyone in Settings › People can be given work in every project.

projectSharing.title: Sharing
projectSharing.notSharedDescription: Work on this project with other people, or on your other PCs, through a folder you already keep in sync with OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive or a network share. Everything {{brand}} writes there is encrypted.
projectSharing.shareThisProjectDescription: {{brand}} makes a new folder for it in OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox, or uses an empty folder you choose. It copies an invite to the clipboard for you to send to the people you share with.
projectSharing.whereToShare: Where should {{brand}} make the shared folder?
projectSharing.anotherFolderHint: An empty folder you keep in sync, such as one on a network drive.
projectSharing.sharedBody: Next, {{folderStep}} Then send them the invite message on your clipboard.
projectSharing.sharedOnServerBody: The invite message is on the clipboard. Send it to the people you share with: anyone with it, who can sign in to the sync server, can open and change this project.
projectSharing.shareOnServerDescription: Kept on {{server}}, encrypted so the server can't read it. Whoever joins needs only the invite, not a folder.

shareFolderStep.google-drive: share the folder "{{folder}}" with them in Google Drive.
shareFolderStep.onedrive: share the folder "{{folder}}" with them in OneDrive.
shareFolderStep.dropbox: share the folder "{{folder}}" with them in Dropbox.
shareFolderStep.folder: give them access to the folder "{{folder}}".

projectSharing.inviteStepSend: Then copy the invite and send it to them by email or chat. Anyone with the invite and the folder can open this project, so send it privately.
projectSharing.inviteServerDescription: Copy the invite and send it to them by email or chat. Anyone with it who can sign in to {{server}} can open this project, so send it privately.
projectSharing.inPersonalSpaceDescription: This project's folder is already in {{place}}. To let someone in, share that folder with them there.
projectSharing.emailSetUpFirst: To email invites from {{brand}}, set up your email server in Settings › Connections › Email.
projectSharing.inviteCopied: Invite copied. Paste it into an email or chat to them.
projectSharing.inviteMessageServer:
Join "{{project}}" in {{brand}}.

1. If you haven't yet, set up the sync server {{server}} in {{brand}}: Settings › Connections › Sync server.
2. Click this link: {{link}}
   If the link doesn't open {{brand}}, choose New project › Join a shared project in {{brand}} and paste this whole message.

inviteFolderStep.google-drive: Open the Google Drive folder "{{folder}}" I shared with you, and choose Organize › Add shortcut to My Drive, so it syncs to your PC.
inviteFolderStep.onedrive: Open the OneDrive folder "{{folder}}" I shared with you, and choose Add shortcut to My files, so it syncs to your PC.
inviteFolderStep.dropbox: Accept the Dropbox folder "{{folder}}" I shared with you, so it syncs to your PC.
inviteFolderStep.folder: Make sure the folder "{{folder}}" I shared with you is on your PC.

projectSharing.awayHint: Only the dates are shared, never the names, and only while they are still ahead.
projectSharing.stopBody: Nothing is deleted. Changes made here will no longer reach the others, and theirs will no longer arrive here.
projectSharing.leaveOnlyYou: Only you leave. The project carries on for everyone else.
projectSharing.leaveKeepCopy: Your copy stays on this PC with everything in it, as a project of your own. Nothing is deleted.

projectSharing.leaveOtherPcs: Your other PCs leave it too, and keep their copies.

projectSharing.leftBody: It's still here, on this PC only.

projectSharing.inviteDriveDescription: First, give each person access below with their Google email address: Google emails them a link to the folder. Then copy the invite and send it to them by email or chat. Anyone with the invite and access to the folder can open this project, so send it privately.

projectCare.repairBody: {{brand}} makes a full backup first. Then it rebuilds the database's indexes, clears links to records that are gone (a task whose milestone is gone keeps the task), and removes records that cannot stand without what they belonged to. If anything goes wrong, restore the backup from Settings › Data.
projectCare.repaired: Repaired: cleared the broken link on {{cleared}} and removed {{removed}}.
projectCare.repairBackup: A full backup from just before is in Settings › Data.
projectCare.checksumFilesDescription: A checksum file (.sha256) beside a file proves later that the file has not changed or been damaged, such as an export copied to a USB drive.
projectCare.writeChecksumFileDescription: For any file: an export, a backup, a document.
projectCare.checkFileDescription: Compares a file with the .sha256 file beside it.

fileVerdict.matches: The file matches its checksum: it has not changed.
fileVerdict.differs: The file does not match its checksum: it has changed or is damaged.
fileVerdict.missing: There is no checksum file beside this file.

projectCare.projectFileDescription: One .ostler-project file with everything, Library files included, that {{brand}} on any computer can open. It can be protected with a password.
projectCare.tasksCsvDescription: Every task with every column, for Excel or another tool.
projectCare.calendarFileDescription: Due dates and milestones as an .ics file for Outlook, Google Calendar or Apple Calendar.
projectCare.webPageDescription: A single page with key numbers, milestones and the task list, to share with anyone.
projectCare.templateDescription: This project as a starting point for new projects.
projectCare.recordsAsFilesDescription: Every record {{brand}} holds for this project, written as JSON files into .ostler-archive in the project's folder.
projectCare.recordsAsFilesNoFolder: Every record {{brand}} holds for this project, written as JSON files into a folder you choose.
projectCare.importTasksDescription: From a CSV file, a Trello board, GitHub issues or a project file, into this project.
projectCare.openProjectFileDescription: A project file or a backup, opened as a new project. This project is not changed.
projectCare.archiveText: Hides the project everywhere but Settings › Projects. Nothing is deleted; bring it back any time.
projectCare.restoreText: This project is hidden everywhere but Settings › Projects. Nothing was deleted.
projectCare.backUpAndRemoveText: Makes a fresh backup of this project, then deletes everything {{brand}} holds for it. The backup opens again as a new project.
projectCare.removePermanentlyText: Deletes everything under "Deleted from this computer" now, without making a new backup. Your existing backups can still bring it back.
projectCare.removePermanentlyNoBackupText: Deletes everything under "Deleted from this computer" now. There is no backup of this project, so it cannot be brought back.
projectCare.guidedHeading: Not sure? Go through it together
projectCare.guidedText: {{brand}} shows what it holds, offers to save the records into your project folder, and asks before each step. You can stop at any point and nothing changes.
projectCare.backupKeptBody: Open it again any time with Import › a project file, or from this folder:
projectCare.checkProjectBackupsFound_one: {{count}} backup, made {{when}}. It stays after removal.
projectCare.checkProjectBackupsFound_other: {{count}} backups, the newest {{when}}. They stay after removal.
projectCare.checkProjectBackupsNone: None yet. A backup opens again as a new project if you change your mind.
projectCare.checkFullBackupsNone: None yet. Settings › Data makes and restores them.
projectCare.checkSecondPlaceFound: Full backups are copied to {{folder}}, last {{when}}.
projectCare.checkSecondPlaceNone: Not set up. Settings › Data can copy full backups to a USB drive or OneDrive.
projectCare.checkArchivesNone: None written. Export and import › Records as JSON files writes them.
projectCare.checkArchivesNoFolder: This project has no folder of its own.
projectCare.deletesRecords: {{records}} in {{tables}}, from {{brand}}'s database file (the file itself stays)

folderKind.agentData: Agent records: sessions, transcripts and their history
folderKind.taskCopies: Agents' copies of the project, one per task

projectCare.keepsFolder: Your project folder and every file in it
projectCare.keepsNoFolder: This project has no folder of its own, so nothing outside {{brand}} is touched.
projectCare.keepsGit_one: Its Git history, and the agent's work on {{count}} ostler/ version
projectCare.keepsGit_other: Its Git history, and the agents' work on {{count}} ostler/ versions
projectCare.keepsBackups: This project's backups and the full backups
projectCare.keepsArchives: The records already written into the project's folder
projectCare.confirmKeeps: Your project folder, its files and its Git history are not touched, and existing backups are kept.
projectCare.confirmBackupFirst: A fresh backup of this project is made first; if that fails, nothing is deleted.
projectCare.confirmNoNewBackup: No new backup is made. The newest backup of this project is from {{when}}: anything since then is lost.
projectCare.confirmNoBackupAtAll: There is no backup of this project. This cannot be undone.

demoLanguage.couldntSwitch: The demo projects couldn’t be switched

demoRemoval.heading: Remove the demo projects
demoRemoval.text: {{projectName}} is one of the two demo projects. This removes both, with everything in them, in one go. Nothing outside {{brand}} is touched, and you can bring them back any time from Ctrl+K: Open the sample project.
demoRemoval.otherWays: Back it up, archive it or remove only this one
demoRemoval.body_one: {{brand}} removes {{names}} and everything in it. Bring it back any time from Ctrl+K: Open the sample project.
demoRemoval.body_other: {{brand}} removes {{names}} and everything in them. Bring them back any time from Ctrl+K: Open the sample project.
demoRemoval.added: You added {{what}} to them, which go too.
demoRemoval.bringBack: Bring them back any time from Ctrl+K: Open the sample project.
